::: {#exm-left-right}
#### Left is not right

The binary trees (@def-binary-tree), with $\operatorname{single}$ as in @rem-single,

$$
\operatorname{node}\paren{x, \operatorname{single}(y), \mathtt{nil}}
\quad \text{and} \quad
\operatorname{node}\paren{x, \mathtt{nil}, \operatorname{single}(y)}
$$

are different: $y$ is the root of the left subtree of the first, and of the right subtree of the second.
@fig-left-right draws them.
As rooted trees (@rem-binary-drawing), they are the same: a root $x$ with one child $y$.
So a binary tree says more than its rooted tree:
it says whether each child is on the left or on the right.

::: {#fig-left-right}

![](../images/trees-left-right.png){fig-alt="Two small trees.
On the left, x with y below it to the left.
On the right, x with y below it to the right." width="40%"}

Two different binary trees with the same rooted tree.
